main_body: A 4x3 tile patch of flat paving: brick-like stone slabs in a staggered running bond, separated by darker mortar lines.
top_band: none. This is a flat ground surface, with no standing volume or top/front split to read in a pixel column.
evidence: The candidate is a terrain paving patch, not a standing object, so the top-plus-front 3/4 contract does not apply. Nothing in it reads as an upright wall or a slab with a missing face. It is a flat ground texture and shows no receding side faces.

style.evidence: Each slab is a large flat fill of one tan-grey, about 7x7 px or bigger. The only variation is a small light highlight at one corner and a dark 2x2 patch at another, repeated identically on every slab. The mortar lines are a tinted dark grey-brown, which is acceptable. The ramp is only about 4 steps (highlight, base, mortar, dark mortar). The Beodeul paving reference has per-stone shading, speckle and cobble grain, so each of its tiles carries many more colours. These tiles are mostly 3-5 colours, which reads as thin, flat and mechanically repeated beside the reference.
